skill.name: Idioms: the meaning isn't the words
skill.why: Idioms are everywhere in talk and stories. Taken literally, they make no sense.
skill.how: Ask: does the plain meaning fit the story? If not, use the clues.

steps.say: Mo told me about my surprise party. Gus said this.

options.text: Mo told the secret.
Mo dropped a tin of beans.
options.reason: Check the clue: the surprise party. Did anyone drop beans?

options.text: Mo cooked beans for the party.
options.reason: Nobody cooked. What happens when someone talks about a surprise?

steps.win: Yes! He told the secret. The clue says secret, not beans.

steps.say: A set saying like that is called an idiom.

show.nudge: Nobody says spilled the peas. An idiom always uses the same words.

show.text: Mo let the cat out of the bag.

show.nudge: That one is plain. It means just what it says.

steps.win: Yes! Same meaning: told the secret. No cat, no bag.

terms.means: A set saying. Its meaning isn't the words, like spill the beans.
Words in the story that show what the saying means.
The same words, but really true, like cold feet from a creek.

creature.name: Archiom
creature.blurb: An archerfish that spits sayings instead of water. Take them literally and you'll miss. Read the clues around them and you'll hit the target.

encounters.frame: Mo is up to his old tricks. The Archiom is trying not to laugh.

encounters.frame: Tully is reading out a story from the Space Club newsletter. The Archiom keeps splashing.
encounters.text: The Space Club had spent six weeks building a model rocket. On launch day, they carried it out to the middle of the footy oval. Jasper was so excited that he grabbed the remote and reached for the big red button. 'Hold your horses!' said Ms Nguyen. 'We haven't checked the wind yet, and Mr Ford is still mowing the far end of the oval.' Jasper's finger froze just above the button. Ms Nguyen licked her finger and held it up. Then she waited until Mr Ford had parked his mower behind the shed. 'Right,' she said. 'Now you can launch.' The rocket shot up so high that it disappeared into a cloud. Nobody has found it yet.

items.reason: 'Flat out' is Aussie for very busy, not lying flat. No lunch break is the clue.

encounters.frame: Gus is telling the crew about his aunt's wedding. The Archiom thinks it sounds fancy.
encounters.text: My aunt got married in a fancy hotel in the city. Before we went in, Mum gave me a serious look. 'Mind your p's and q's tonight,' she said. So I did. I said please and thank you to every waiter. I put my napkin on my lap and chewed with my mouth closed. I didn't burp once, not even after the fizzy drink. I even asked the lady next to me how her day had been. Then she asked me about my hobbies, so I told her all about my fish-guts experiment. She moved to another table. Mum says I did really well until dessert.
encounters.prompt: What does Mum mean by 'Mind your p's and q's'?
encounters.success: Use your best manners. So Gus says please and thank you, and doesn't burp once.

options.text: Use your very best manners.
Stay quiet and don't talk to anyone.
options.reason: Gus chats to the lady next to him, and Mum says he did well. What else did he do?

options.text: Eat everything that is on your plate.
options.reason: Mum never mentions food. Think about please, thank you and no burping.

encounters.frame: Wren wrote about the first morning of reef camp. The Archiom was there too.
encounters.text: On the first morning of reef camp, twelve kids who had never met sat in a circle on the dive boat. Nobody said a word. Some stared at their flippers. One boy read the safety sign for ten whole minutes. Mo, the camp cook, was busy with the drinks. The ice in the cooler had frozen into one big block, so he broke the ice with a hammer. Nobody even looked up. Then Mo carried out a plate of his fish-finger custard. 'Who wants to be brave first?' he asked. One girl laughed, then another. Soon everyone was arguing about whether fish fingers belonged anywhere near custard. By lunchtime, the whole group was chatting and swapping stories. 'You really broke the ice this morning,' the camp leader told Mo, watching the kids laugh together. Mo was so pleased that he made a second batch. Nobody ate that one either.
encounters.prompt: What does the camp leader mean when she says Mo 'really broke the ice'?
encounters.success: He got everyone talking. She says it while the kids laugh together, not when he smashed the cooler ice.

options.text: He smashed the frozen block in the drinks cooler.
options.reason: He did, but nobody even looked up. She says it while watching the kids laugh together.

options.text: He got the kids relaxed and talking to each other.
He made the awkward silence on the boat even worse.
options.reason: After the custard, the kids laugh and chat. The silence ended.

options.text: He started an argument that upset the whole group.
options.reason: They argued about custard, but in a fun way. By lunchtime they were all chatting.

encounters.frame: Gus wrote a note about the Great Biscuit Argument. One word is wrong.
encounters.text: It started with one chocolate biscuit. There was only one left in the tin, and Tully and Zed both reached for it at the same moment. Tully said she had called it at breakfast. encounters.frame: Tully is telling the crew about Sunday lunch at her nan's. The Archiom is under the table.
encounters.text: Every Sunday, my whole family squeezes around Nan's table for roast chicken. Last Sunday, my little cousin Archie decided he was a comedian. Before lunch, he leaned right out of the front window to yell at a dog, until Uncle Ray pulled him back inside. At the table, he said the gravy was the colour of swamp water. When Uncle Ray told a fishing story, Archie yawned loudly and said, 'Wake me up when the fish gets away.' Then he poked Nan's famous pudding with his spoon and asked if it was meant to be that colour. Everyone went quiet. Nan put down her spoon, looked at Archie over her glasses and said, 'Pull your head in, young man.' Archie went bright red. He said sorry to Nan, ate two bowls of pudding without another word, and even offered to do the dishes. Nan gave him a third bowl. That's how you know she has forgiven you.
encounters.prompt: What does Nan mean when she tells Archie to pull his head in?
encounters.success: Stop being cheeky. Archie insults the food and the stories, then says sorry, so Nan was telling him off.

options.text: Bring your head back in from the window.
options.reason: That was before lunch, and Uncle Ray already pulled him in. Now he's at the table.

options.text: Stop daydreaming and listen to me.
options.reason: Archie isn't daydreaming. Think about the comments he keeps making.

options.text: Stop being cheeky and rude to everyone.
Stop being shy and join in more.
options.reason: Archie isn't shy at all. He keeps making loud jokes about the food.

encounters.frame: Tully wrote up the Year 6 relay race for the school newsletter. The Archiom is still laughing.
encounters.text: The Year 6 relay was the last race of the athletics carnival, and the Blue team was in the lead. Ruby was running the final leg. She stood in her lane, bouncing on her toes, waiting for Eli to bring her the baton. When Eli was still halfway down the track, Ruby heard the crowd cheering and thought it was for her. She took off, sprinting as hard as she could, all the way to the finish line. She crossed it with her arms in the air, before Eli had even reached the changeover. Then she turned around and saw that her hands were empty. Eli was standing at the changeover, holding out the baton to nobody. 'You jumped the gun,' said Coach Ellis, shaking her head. Ruby had to walk all the way back and run the leg again. Blue came third, but Ruby still says she ran the fastest leg of the day, twice.
encounters.prompt: What does Coach Ellis mean when she says Ruby jumped the gun?
encounters.success: She went too soon. Ruby left before Eli gave her the baton, and there's no starter's gun mid-race.

options.text: Ruby ran before the starter's gun went off.
options.reason: The starter's gun goes at the start of the race. Ruby ran the last leg, waiting for Eli.

options.text: Ruby set off running before it was her turn.
Ruby ran faster than anyone else in the race.
options.reason: She did run fast, but Coach is shaking her head. Look at when Ruby left.

options.text: Ruby ignored the plan her coach had given her.
options.reason: Coach never mentions a plan. Look at when Ruby left: before Eli reached her.

encounters.frame: Indi found this letter in the Soggy Biscuit's mailbag. The Archiom is drying it out.
encounters.text: Dear Aunty Bec, Guess what? My team won the Junior Space Challenge! We had to design a base for astronauts living on the Moon, with enough water, food and air for four people for a whole year, and then present it to a panel of real scientists. The competition was on Friday morning, and on Monday we still hadn't finished. So for the last four nights, we burned the midnight oil. Every evening after dinner, the three of us crowded around the kitchen table at Priya's house, surrounded by cardboard tubes and glue, working until nearly midnight while her parents brought us cups of hot chocolate. The lights were on the whole time, so we could see every tiny piece. On Thursday night, Priya's dad found us asleep on top of the model, with glue in our hair. We slept in on Friday morning and nearly missed the bus, but we made it, and the judges said our water recycling tank was the cleverest design they had seen all year. The prize is a trip to the space centre in the holidays. Mum says next time we should start earlier, and she is probably right. Priya's dad says next time we should use less glue. Love, Ava
encounters.prompt: Ava's team burned the midnight oil. Which of these is also burning the midnight oil?
encounters.success: Gus is working hard late at night to finish a job, just like Ava's team did.

options.text: Mo getting up at four o'clock to bake bread for the whole crew.
options.reason: It's hard work, but it's early in the morning. Ava's team worked late at night.

options.text: Gus fixing the engine until midnight so the boat can leave at dawn.
Zed staying up until midnight to watch the New Year fireworks.
options.reason: It's late, but it's fun. Ava's team stayed up working hard to finish a job.

options.text: Tully lighting an oil lamp at night when the power goes out.
options.reason: That's the plain meaning. Ava says the lights were on, so nothing was really burning.

parts: Mangrove Rafters is a two-player game where you steer a raft through a maze of channels, collecting gold coins and dodging crocodiles. Whoever reaches the finish line first wins the Golden Paddle. Zed and Gus had been playing it all afternoon.

parts.tap: Their raft floated slowly up the creek, past a sleeping crocodile.
parts.reason: This makes the plain meaning more likely, not less. They really are on a creek.

parts: Gus steered like a learner driver on his very first day. Then, on the very last level, everything went wrong at once. A storm hit, a log smashed into their raft, and they lost their last two lives to a crocodile they hadn't noticed.

parts.tap: Their health bar was flashing red, and the final boss, a giant mud crab, was scuttling towards them.
parts.reason: This shows they're in trouble, so it hints at the meaning. It doesn't show the words aren't true.

parts.tap: Both paddles were still in the raft, but that didn't help one bit.

parts: They were well and truly up the creek without a paddle.

parts.tap: Zed pressed every button on the controller as he tried to escape.
parts.reason: This shows Zed panicking. It doesn't tell you whether they had paddles.

parts: The crab caught them three metres from the finish line. GAME OVER flashed across the screen in huge red letters. Gus put the controller down very carefully, walked out onto the deck and stared at the real mangroves for a long time. Zed pressed restart. 'Best of three,' he called out. Gus didn't come back inside until dinner, and even then he wouldn't look at the console.

encounters.frame: Tully wrote a note about Mo's family lunch. One part is wrong.
encounters.text: For Nan's eightieth birthday, Mo offered to make the dessert, and the family was too polite to say no. He decided on a pavlova, a giant one, decorated with kiwi fruit and passionfruit. Unfortunately, he left it in the oven for three hours instead of one. When he carried it out to the table, it was black on top and smoking slightly, and the whole house smelled of smoke. Nobody said a word about it. Nan talked about her new hat, which had a feather in it. Uncle Ray talked about the weather, and how much rain they'd had in March. Aunty Jo talked about her neighbour's dog, which had learned to open the fridge. Everyone cut themselves a tiny slice of the black pavlova and pushed it slowly around their plates, while they talked and talked about anything else. The burnt pavlova was the elephant in the room, sitting right in the middle of the table. At last, Mo's little cousin Pip, who was four, pointed at it and said, 'Why is the cake on fire?' Everyone burst out laughing, including Mo, and Nan said it was the most memorable birthday cake she had ever had. They ordered pizza.

encounters.frame: The Archiom has been eavesdropping on the crew all week.
encounters.prompt: Match each idiom to what it means. Check how they felt and what they did.
encounters.success: Put two clues together: how they felt, and what they did next. That told you each meaning.

items.text: Tully missed kicks for three hours, then threw in the towel and went inside.
items.reason: She tried for hours, then stopped. Nothing says she was scared, just done.

items.text: Zed got cold feet about the show. His hands shook, and by breakfast his name was off the list.
items.reason: Shaking hands show fear, and taking his name off shows he pulled out.

items.text: Wren's hands shook, but she bit the bullet and rang the vet.
items.reason: Her hands shook, but she still rang. Scared, but she did it.

items.text: Gus called it quits after his sixth experiment fizzled out, and packed his test tubes away.
items.reason: Packing away the test tubes after six tries shows he stopped trying.

items.text: Mo's knees were knocking, but he took the plunge and walked on stage.
items.reason: Knocking knees show fear, but he walked on stage anyway.

items.text: Zed knew he was in deep water when Mr Lee found the drawing and rang his parents.
items.reason: He's not swimming. A teacher ringing your parents means trouble.

encounters.frame: Maxx Vantablack is live, and he is not happy. Zed is recording it for evidence.
encounters.text: Vantafam, Maxx here, and today I need to talk about something serious. Some of you have been leaving comments saying my rescues are fake. Fake! Me! After everything I've done for the Creatures of this archipelago! One person said the swamp behind me is painted on a board. Another said they could see a camera crew in the reflection of my sunnies. Someone even said the Creature I rescued last week had a price tag on its tail. Come on, guys, fair crack of the whip! I have spent six years building this channel. I have rescued more Creatures than anyone in history, probably. I deserve a chance to show you what I really do before you start writing nasty comments about me. So this week, I'm doing something special. I'm going to film a rescue from start to finish, with no editing at all, so you can all see for yourselves. Well, a little bit of editing. For the lighting. And the sound. And maybe a couple of the bits in the middle. But apart from that, totally real. Smash that heart button if you believe in me, and remember, two Xs, because one X is for losers. Stay gold!
encounters.prompt: Why is it funny when Maxx asks for a 'fair crack of the whip'?
encounters.success: Maxx wants a fair chance to prove his rescues are real. Then he admits he'll edit the 'unedited' video.

options.text: He wants the people who doubt him punished with a real whip.
options.reason: That's the plain meaning. Maxx wants a chance to show his rescues, not a punishment.

options.text: He has rescued more Creatures than anyone else in history.
options.reason: That's only Maxx's claim, and he says 'probably'. The joke is about the chance he asks for.

options.text: He wants a fair chance, then admits the 'real' video is edited.
He asks his viewers to hurry up and make up their minds.
options.reason: He asks them to wait and watch first. Look at what he admits about the video.

encounters.frame: Tully is telling the crew about a family mystery. The Archiom has its fins crossed.
encounters.text: In my grandpa's lounge room, there is a glass cabinet full of footy trophies, and right in the middle stands the biggest one of all, the 1978 Mangrove Cup. It has a crack running all the way down one side, and someone has glued the handle back on, a bit crooked. Nobody in my family will say how it happened. Last weekend, while Grandpa was out walking his dog, I asked Gran about it. She was sitting on the back step, shelling peas. She stopped for a moment, looked at the cabinet through the window, and then went back to her peas. 'Some things are better left alone, love,' she said. 'Let sleeping dogs lie.' I tried asking Uncle Ray instead, but he suddenly remembered he had to mow the lawn, even though he had mowed it that morning. Aunty Jo just laughed until she had to sit down. When Grandpa came home with the dog, I opened my mouth to ask him, and Gran gave me a very stern look. So I closed it again. I still don't know what happened to that trophy, but I have a feeling Grandpa does. And I have a feeling it's a very good story.
encounters.prompt: Gran says 'Let sleeping dogs lie.' What does saying it this way let her do?
encounters.success: She stops Tully asking, but tells her nothing about the trophy. The idiom keeps the secret safe.

options.text: Tell Tully, kindly, that the dog cracked the trophy.
options.reason: Gran never says how the trophy cracked. The sleeping dogs are part of the idiom.

options.text: Make Tully laugh so she forgets all about the trophy.
options.reason: Aunty Jo laughs, not Gran. Gran is serious and later gives a stern look.

options.text: Warn Tully that Grandpa's dog bites if it is woken.
options.reason: That's the plain meaning. The dog is out walking with Grandpa, not asleep.

options.text: Stop Tully asking, without giving away any of the secret.
